UnitStatement: The deliverable-consistency skill is used with the generic TASK shell.
A deliverable-consistency brief requires ScopePath.
A deliverable-consistency brief requires TaskSkill: deliverable-consistency.
A deliverable-consistency brief requires RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH.
A deliverable-consistency task can perform a contradiction sweep.
A deliverable-consistency task can review unresolved TBD, ASSUMPTION, and CONFLICT markers.
A deliverable-consistency task can propose identity normalization.
A deliverable-consistency task can review source and evidence completeness.
ApplyEdits: false is the normal safe default for deliverable-consistency.
ApplyEdits: true should be used only for clearly desired minimal corrections with authorized writable targets.
A valid deliverable-consistency run requires the deliverable path to exist.
The deterministic scan must complete unless tool use was explicitly excluded.
Deliverable-consistency findings must reference only files inside the deliverable.
Each significant deliverable-consistency finding must include a best-effort evidence location.
Contradictions must be surfaced as rulings-needed items rather than silently resolved.
Applied edits must be limited to files authorized by the effective bounded task brief.
MEMORY.md may capture durable decisions or accepted proposals only when the brief authorizes that update.
Recommended deliverable-consistency reporting groups include identity mismatch findings.
Recommended deliverable-consistency reporting groups include unresolved marker findings.
Recommended deliverable-consistency reporting groups include contradiction findings.
Recommended deliverable-consistency reporting groups include unsourced numeric parameter findings.
Recommended deliverable-consistency reporting groups include missing artifact and missing reference findings.
A no-findings success case must explicitly state that no material consistency findings were discovered in scope.
A no-findings success case should mention residual risk if references are sparse or artifacts are missing.
The deliverable-consistency skill runs a deliverable-local consistency sweep across production documents in one deliverable.
The deliverable-consistency skill works with generic TASK briefs that identify exactly one deliverable folder.
The deliverable-consistency skill helps surface contradictions.
The deliverable-consistency skill helps find unresolved TBD, ASSUMPTION, and CONFLICT markers.
The deliverable-consistency skill helps identify unsourced numeric parameters.
The deliverable-consistency skill helps spot identity mismatches across the document set.
The deliverable-consistency skill helps propose minimal corrective edits when authorized.
The suitable shell for deliverable-consistency is TASK in generic shell mode with no profile.
The deliverable-consistency skill requires ScopePath.
The deliverable-consistency skill requires RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH.
Tasks is an optional deliverable-consistency input.
RuntimeOverrides.FocusDocs is an optional deliverable-consistency input.
RuntimeOverrides.Strictness is an optional deliverable-consistency input.
RuntimeOverrides.MaxFindings is an optional deliverable-consistency input.
RuntimeOverrides.CheckIdentity is an optional deliverable-consistency input.
RuntimeOverrides.CheckUnsourcedNumerics is an optional deliverable-consistency input.
FocusDocs limits the sweep to named production documents and defaults to all production documents.
Strictness accepts conservative or aggressive finding posture and defaults to conservative.
MaxFindings is a soft cap on reported findings and defaults to 10.
CheckIdentity checks folder and document naming consistency and defaults to true.
CheckUnsourcedNumerics flags numeric statements needing evidence review and defaults to true.
The preferred deterministic helper is tools/validation/scan_deliverable_consistency.py.
The preferred deliverable-consistency method runs the deterministic scan first.
The preferred deliverable-consistency method reads only flagged deliverable-local files and nearby context.
The preferred deliverable-consistency method compares files directly where the deterministic scan cannot decide.
Deliverable-consistency output should be recommendation-first unless edits are explicitly authorized.
The deliverable-consistency task must not widen scope beyond the single deliverable.
The deliverable-consistency task must not edit outside the effective bounded task brief write authorization.
The deliverable-consistency task must not silently resolve conflicts.
Deliverable-consistency outputs include PROPOSAL blocks for consistency issues.
Deliverable-consistency outputs include MISSING items where files or references are absent.
Deliverable-consistency outputs include NEEDS_HUMAN_RULING items for true contradictions.
Deliverable-consistency outputs may include applied minimal edits only if ApplyEdits is true.
Deliverable-consistency outputs may include a MEMORY.md update only when the brief explicitly authorizes it.
Every deliverable-consistency finding must cite a file and best-effort section or heading.
Unknowns must remain TBD.
Conflicts must be surfaced rather than silently reconciled.
Proposed deliverable-consistency edits should be minimal and reversible.
Deliverable-consistency findings must be scoped to one deliverable.
The deterministic scan should run first unless the brief explicitly forbids tool use.
Deliverable-consistency findings should be grouped by issue type where practical.
Identity mismatches and unresolved markers must be explicitly reported when found.
A deliverable-consistency run with no meaningful issues should say so explicitly rather than padding output.
The deliverable-consistency tool policy is tool-first for the initial sweep and reasoning-first for adjudication.
The preferred tool order starts by running tools/validation/scan_deliverable_consistency.py against the deliverable.
The preferred tool order then reads flagged production documents and nearby context.
The preferred tool order then compares files directly where the scan surfaces a plausible inconsistency.
The preferred tool order then emits evidence-backed proposals.
The preferred tool order applies minimal edits only if authorized.
The normal scan invocation is python3 tools/validation/scan_deliverable_consistency.py "$DELIVERABLE_PATH".
Optional scan flags should be used only when the brief calls for them.
The TASK-enforced allowed tool is python3 tools/validation/scan_deliverable_consistency.py:*.
No additional operational helpers are declared beyond the TASK-enforced scanner.
The deterministic scan is a first-pass detector, not a final judge.
Unresolved markers are deterministic findings.
Identity mismatches are candidate inconsistencies until checked in context.
Unsourced numeric lines are review prompts, not automatic defects.
Reasoning takes over after the deterministic sweep by reading flagged docs, comparing files directly, and producing evidence-backed proposals and human-ruling items.
Hidden reliance on tools outside the declared list is disallowed unless the human expands AllowedTools.
Writes outside declared scope are disallowed.
Project-wide scanning is disallowed.
Widening scope beyond the single deliverable is disallowed.
Edits outside authorization are disallowed.
Silent conflict resolution is disallowed.
Dependency register edits are disallowed unless separately authorized by the brief.
Writes are limited to the effective bounded task brief write authorization for the single deliverable.
Optional applied minimal edits require ApplyEdits: true.
MEMORY.md updates and dependency register edits require explicit brief authorization.
